# Appendix E. Geographic decisions and origin-destination flows

## E1 Reading the geographic results

The maps in this appendix locate the investments in each accepted planning
solution. An orange circle denotes a candidate warehouse that is opened, a red
square denotes an expansion, and a magenta diamond denotes conversion to bulk
handling. Purple stars identify **export ports**. A warehouse can receive more
than one investment, and different facilities can share coordinates. Their CDA
identifiers remain separate in the investment tables even when symbols overlap.

An opened candidate, installed capacity and operational use answer different
questions. Opening is a binary investment decision; installed capacity is a
quantity in tonnes; use is established by a positive exported flow. For an
existing warehouse, the original availability flag does not signify a new
opening. Likewise, the bulk-handling investment basis is not additional static
storage. The tables distinguish candidate storage, static expansion and the
basis used to calculate handling gains.

The configuration summaries count positive investment quantities above
$10^{-7}$ t. Binary activation flags and the original quantities are retained
separately in the complete lists, allowing activation without material capacity
to be distinguished from a positive investment. This display threshold does
not replace the original feasibility tolerances.

Each map is presented individually. All maps use the same national extent and
IBGE boundary dataset, with attribution retained in the image. The paragraph
following each figure explains its projection and interpretation. Companion
capacity views use circle area proportional to added candidate plus expansion
storage, measured in tonnes. Original facility coordinates are retained.

The configurations comprise the deterministic and stochastic warehouse-only
plans, the larger stochastic populations, the two h215 plans permitting direct
origin-destination movements, and the accepted Pyomo solutions. The historical native-Gurobi h300 runs
with 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 solver threads have byte-identical original warehouse,
flow, inventory and shortage exports. Their common investment map and flow
matrices are therefore represented by the single-thread vector; their runtime
observations remain distinct. The accepted Pyomo Gurobi and HiGHS solutions
retain their own exported vectors, attained gaps and investment summaries.
The two common-Pyomo h300 pilots are separate observations. Their own
maps and investment lists follow the historical configurations; their full
flow-distance companions retain separate source and solution identities.

## E2 From exported flows to sparse matrices

Let $x^{k}_{ijpts}$ denote the exported tonnes on directed movement family $k$,
from endpoint $i$ to endpoint $j$, for product $p$, period $t$ and scenario $s$.
The full-resolution companion retains these indices and the original
probability $\pi_s$. Its expected-horizon matrix is

$$
F^{k,p}_{ij}=\sum_{s\in S}\pi_s\sum_{t\in T}x^{k}_{ijpts}.
$$

For a deterministic solution there is one scenario with probability one. For
the reported stochastic configurations, nine Cartesian supply-demand scenarios
each have probability $1/9$. The aggregation sums transported tonnes over the
original 60 monthly periods. It neither annualizes the quantities nor treats
different scenarios as successive physical shipments.

The paired distance matrix is $D^k_{ij}=d^k_{ij}$, where $d^k_{ij}$ is the OSRM
road distance in kilometres in the exact processed workbook used by that
configuration. Distances are joined by **movement family and directed endpoint
identities**, never by the order of rows or by geographic proximity. A
destination's domestic or export role is retained separately. Reversing a
movement requires its own recorded distance. Distances are not summed when
periods or scenarios are aggregated.

The implementation's legacy family codes are OD for origin-warehouse, DD for
warehouse-warehouse, DC for warehouse-destination, and OC for a direct
origin-destination movement. Thus, the code OD does not mean a direct
origin-customer movement. OC occurs only in the D configurations. The
warehouse-only W configurations do not admit that movement family.

The companions use coordinate-form sparse matrices: each row names the product,
directed endpoints, movement family, expected tonnes and OSRM kilometres. The
unaggregated companion also gives period, scenario, probability and original
tonnes. This representation preserves the positive flows without printing
large mostly empty rectangular arrays. Summing all movement families would
double-count grain transported through successive network legs; domestic and
export arrivals must instead be evaluated at their appropriate destinations.

The original exporter omits flow magnitudes at or below $10^{-7}$ t. An absent
row therefore must not be treated as proof of an exact zero or as evidence that
an arc was inadmissible. Zero flow, an arc excluded by screening, an unexported
small value and missing road geometry are distinct states. Reconstructing the
complete admissibility mask requires the frozen network definition identified
with the input data. All positive records in the prepared companions have an
exact matching workbook distance; no distance or road polyline is interpolated.

These are **flows of accepted solutions**, rather than claims of exact
zero-gap optima. Each configuration below retains its attained relative
objective gap. The original independent primal certificates were accepted;
post-processing their exports does not constitute a new optimization or a
fresh residual check.

The [configuration and original-export index](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/0788de130253dddc790b179c8831d8ee29dabcbd/manuscript/supplement/appendix_e_sources.json),
[numerical companion inventory](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/0788de130253dddc790b179c8831d8ee29dabcbd/manuscript/supplement/appendix_e_summary.json)
and [reconstruction program](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/0788de130253dddc790b179c8831d8ee29dabcbd/scripts/build_appendix_e.py)
identify the precise versions and aggregation procedure. The complete warehouse
lists are linked under each configuration. Full-resolution flow-distance tables
are prepared as compressed CSVs and a separate SQLite database; they are not
currently public GitHub downloads. Access to their processed-source data and
redistribution conditions follows the availability statement in Appendix D.
The software license does not by itself establish unrestricted input-data access.

The versioned delivery sequence in Appendix D11 applies to these companions:
the present GitHub indices identify their contents and original sources,
while the planned Zenodo version will provide reviewed full-resolution files.
They are currently prepared locally, not newly deposited. Original coordinate
rows and scenario weights remain available in the companions rather than
being replaced by a rendered map. Later campaign records without a usable
incumbent have no investment map or flow matrix to contribute.
